A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MASS, with matching core algorithms and retained vision benchmarks. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-merging experiments, router comparisons, layer analyses, batched-inference results and task-vector interpretations, including supplementary results.

after.justification: V2 reports original vision and language evaluations, scalability and held-out-task experiments, and component and sensitivity analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The fixed and adaptive merging algorithms retain TSV compression, orthogonalization, redundancy filtering, residual routing and classification across selected heads. V1 Algorithms 1–2 correspond to v2 Algorithms 2–1. Unknown-task head selection already appears in v1 Section 3.3; the additional experimental variants do not replace the proposed method.

E1.justification: V2 retains the 8/14/20-task vision benchmarks and adds 13 vision datasets for scaling to 33 tasks, eight GLUE language tasks, and evaluation on tasks excluded from merging. These substantially broaden the domains and generalization scenarios beyond v1's vision evaluations.

E2.justification: V2 Table 1 adds evaluated WeMoE and SMILE-1/2 comparisons; v1 discussed these approaches without reporting corresponding experiments. V2 Table 2 also evaluates TIES-Merging on GLUE. The original fixed-merging baselines, TwinMerging comparison and alternative-router comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include Flan-T5-Base merging, majority-vote head selection for SMILE/WeMoE (Appendix B.6), oracle-head controls (Table 11), and merging seven experts before testing the excluded task (Appendix C.1). These are added protocols; unknown-task inference for MASS was already present in v1.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained layer, router and semantic analyses, v2 tests unseen-task transfer, scalability, residual-weighted merging, orthogonalization, oracle heads, routing/filtering sensitivity, Mahalanobis distance and principal-angle filtering. Tables 7–13 and Figures 6 and 10 substantially expand evidence about component choices, robustness and failure conditions.

E5.justification: V2 Table 14 newly reports means and standard deviations across tasks for the main MoErging comparisons. V1 already reports cross-task variability in routing-layer plots. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests; the added deviations describe task heterogeneity.

E6.justification: Main vision, router and batched-inference results are revised, alongside substantial new results. For example, v1 Table 2 reports MASS at 90.6% absolute/97.6% normalized accuracy for eight-task ViT-B-32; v2 Table 1 reports 87.0%/96.5%, with the fine-tuned reference also revised. V2 adds GLUE results and 33-task results of 0.83 versus Task Arithmetic's 0.64. The PDFs do not explain the revisions sufficiently to establish a controlled performance change.

T1.justification: V2 Section 3.4 and Proposition D.2 add a conditional MAP interpretation and proof for residual-based selection, assuming common isotropic Gaussian residuals and uniform task priors. This extends the justification of an existing operation. V1's orthogonal-projection optimality theorem and proof are retained as Proposition D.1.

C1.justification: The central training-free, data-free MASS contribution remains. V2's introduction extends the demonstrated scope to language and replaces v1's across-scale within-5% and batched below-1% claims with an 'up to 98%' statement. Automatic head selection becomes more prominent but was already explicitly claimed in v1.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations linking held-out performance to transferable subspaces, scalability to task composition, and weaker NLI results to potentially diffuse, higher-rank updates. It also explains threshold-related failures, qualifies orthogonalization's contribution as modest, and discusses why alternative distance and filtering choices underperform. These substantially extend v1's mechanism discussion.

D1.justification: V2 adds baseline head-voting instructions, new dataset counts and fallback split instructions, and compute/storage accounting in Appendix B. The existing checkpoint sources, EMNIST preprocessing, shared classification head, MLP architecture, compression rate, hyperparameter searches and code address are retained.

R1.justification: V2 shifts the central positioning from fixed aggregation and task interference toward the absence of oracle task knowledge. It newly argues that known-task merging is effectively addressed by TSV-C compression and foregrounds this distinction from existing MoErging methods. New references support the probabilistic interpretation, language evaluation and added datasets; much of v1's related work survives in Appendix A.

P1.justification: The introduction and results narrative are substantially rewritten, the background is condensed, and detailed related work and the fixed-merging algorithm move to appendices. Benchmark descriptions and batched-inference discussion are reorganized, alongside a new reproducibility statement and restructured appendices.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a single-column conference layout, combines routing-layer panels, rebuilds radar comparisons around MoErging baselines, and relocates algorithms and figures. New language, resource and ablation tables, plus scalability and sensitivity plots, substantially change the visual presentation beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses an important weakness in v1's evaluation by adding direct MoErging competitors, documented head-routing adaptations and oracle-head controls. Component ablations, sensitivity tests and broader evaluations substantially strengthen the evidence for the method's usefulness and design choices. Unexplained score revisions and inconsistencies remain, including the retained 97.6% prose figure versus 96.5% in Table 1 and the miscounted GLUE wins, but the expanded comparative and diagnostic evidence provides a substantial net improvement.
